content.title: Similar Figures and Proportional Sides
content.overview: Similarity in geometry means two figures have the same shape but not necessarily the same size. When figures are similar, their corresponding angles are equal and their corresponding side lengths are proportional. This lesson focuses on identifying corresponding parts and using the scale factor to calculate missing side lengths.
learning_objectives: Identify corresponding vertices and sides in similar polygons.
Calculate the scale factor (k) between two similar figures.
Apply the scale factor to find missing side lengths in a target figure.
Verify similarity by comparing ratios of corresponding side lengths.

sections.title: Understanding Similarity and Correspondence
sections.content: Two figures are similar if one is a scaled version of the other. The order of vertices in a similarity statement (e.g., Triangle ABC ~ Triangle DEF) is critical because it defines the correspondence. Vertex A corresponds to D, B to E, and C to F. Consequently, side AB corresponds to DE, BC to EF, and AC to DF. You must always match sides based on these vertex pairs rather than just looking at the visual orientation of the shapes, as figures may be rotated or reflected.

sections.title: The Scale Factor (k)
sections.content:
The scale factor, denoted as k, represents the constant ratio of all corresponding side lengths. To find k when moving from Figure A to Figure B, use the formula: k = (Side Length in Figure B) ÷ (Corresponding Side Length in Figure A). If k > 1, the figure is an enlargement; if k < 1, it is a reduction. Once k is determined, any missing side in Figure B can be found by multiplying its corresponding side in Figure A by k.

![A flowchart showing the steps: Match Vertices, Calculate Scale Factor k, Multiply Known Side by k, and Verify Ratios.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/2bf8771d-daec-47f3-833c-af929f443366-1786505955287-665.webp)

sections.title: Verification and Proportionality
sections.content: In similar figures, the ratio of any two corresponding sides must be equal. This is expressed as the proportion: (Side 1 of B / Side 1 of A) = (Side 2 of B / Side 2 of A). If you have multiple side lengths, you can verify your work by ensuring that every pair of corresponding sides yields the same scale factor k.

worked_examples.question: Triangle ABC is similar to triangle DEF. The vertices correspond as A↔D, B↔E, and C↔F. In triangle ABC, side AB = 6 and side BC = 8. In triangle DEF, side DE = 9. Find the length of side EF.
worked_examples.solution:
Step 1: Establish correspondence. Based on the vertex mapping, side AB corresponds to DE, and side BC corresponds to EF.
Step 2: Calculate the scale factor (k) using the known pair (AB and DE). k = DE / AB = 9 / 6 = 1.5.
Step 3: Apply the scale factor to find the missing side EF. EF = k × BC = 1.5 × 8 = 12.
Step 4: Final check. The ratio 9/6 (1.5) equals the ratio 12/8 (1.5), confirming the sides are proportional.

common_mistakes: Matching sides based on visual 'position' rather than vertex order, which fails if a shape is rotated.
Inverting the scale factor (dividing Figure A by Figure B when trying to find a side in Figure B).
Assuming figures are similar just because they look alike without a similarity statement or given proportional ratios.
Confusing similarity with congruence; similar figures have proportional sides, not necessarily equal sides.
exam_tips: Always write out the vertex pairs (e.g., A-D, B-E) before performing any calculations.
If the scale factor is a fraction, keep it as a fraction (like 3/2) to avoid rounding errors that occur with decimals.
Look for 'hidden' similar triangles, such as a smaller triangle nested inside a larger one sharing a common angle.
content.recap: Similarity requires that all corresponding angles are congruent and all corresponding sides are proportional. By identifying the vertex correspondence and calculating the scale factor (k = Image / Original), you can solve for any missing side length in a geometric figure.

knowledge_claims.content: Similar figures have the same shape and proportional side lengths, but not necessarily the same size.
In a similarity statement like ABC ~ DEF, the order of letters dictates which vertices and sides correspond to each other.
The scale factor k is calculated by dividing a side length in the target figure by the corresponding side length in the original figure.
To find a missing side in a target similar figure, multiply the corresponding side from the original figure by the scale factor k.
A scale factor k greater than 1 indicates the target figure is larger than the original, while a k between 0 and 1 indicates it is smaller.
Similarity can be verified by checking if the ratios of all pairs of corresponding sides are equal to the same constant k.
Corresponding sides are the segments connecting corresponding pairs of vertices in two similar polygons.
It is a mistake to assume the shortest side of one triangle corresponds to the shortest side of another unless similarity is established.
Unlike congruent figures which have equal side lengths, similar figures have side lengths that maintain a constant ratio.
If triangle ABC ~ DEF, then the ratio AB/DE must equal the ratio BC/EF.
When solving for a missing side, the first step is to identify the known corresponding side pair to establish the scale factor.
Corresponding angles in similar figures are always congruent (equal in measure).
